title: OpenAI nears $30 billion bridge round at $1.25 trillion valuation
subtitle: CNBC reports a round led by UAE-linked investors and Coatue, pitched at a lower valuation than the $1.4 trillion OpenAI floated to backers earlier in October.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: OpenAI is closing on a round of up to $30 billion at a $1.25 trillion pre-money valuation, according to CNBC reporting that broke on October 22. The round is reportedly led by UAE-linked investors and Coatue, and OpenAI has told backers it aims to secure signatures by the end of next week. The company's prior round, in March, priced it at $852 billion.

The valuation itself is the news inside the news. Earlier in October, OpenAI had been circulating a $1.4 trillion number to prospective investors including BlackRock and UAE fund MGX. A $1.25 trillion mark is still a near-50% jump from March, but it is a visible step down from what the company was asking a few weeks ago — a signal that even a company this hot has to meet the market where it is.

Reporting frames this as a bridge round ahead of an IPO. OpenAI filed a confidential prospectus in June and has not disclosed a listing date; CFO Sarah Friar has previously told employees that an IPO could happen in 2027. Bridge rounds at this scale buy time against the capex curve — the compute and data-center commitments that the whole frontier-model business is now carrying — rather than funding new product lines.

A note for learners: a trillion-dollar private valuation is a bet on who gets to run the compute, not on who has the best model today. OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, and the Chinese labs are all raising or committing on the same assumption — that frontier training is going to cost tens of billions of dollars per generation. Watch the funding and the power contracts; that is where the next two years actually get decided.
